questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the right lane will end.

questions.question: When riding behind a car in the left third of the lane, the driver can see you in their side mirror. What is one problem with this position?

options.text: Most drivers look at their rearview mirror more often than their side mirror.
Wind can block the side mirror.
Drivers should never use their side mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most drivers look at their rearview mirror more often than their side mirror.
questions.explanation: Most drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors. When following a car, ride in the center of the lane. This way, the driver is more likely to see you in their rearview mirror.

questions.question: A motorcycle's horn is ________ a car's horn.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's horn is not as loud as a car's horn. Use your horn when needed, but do not rely on it to stay safe.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while braking on dry pavement, you should:

options.text: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and quickly re-apply it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If the rear wheel locks while you stop on dry pavement, you can keep it locked. You can still control your motorcycle if it is upright and going straight, even with a locked rear wheel.

questions.question: To make it easier for other drivers to see you, you should:
questions.explanation: Wearing bright-colored clothing makes it easier for other drivers to see you. This works day or night.

questions.question: Service signs are:
questions.explanation: Blue signs with white letters show where services are located. These services include rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: In areas where dangers could happen, a motorcyclist should:

options.text: Keep riding at the same speed.
Keep your fingers on the clutch and both brakes to react faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your fingers on the clutch and both brakes to react faster.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like intersections, shopping areas, schools, or construction zones, slow down. Keep your fingers on the clutch and both brakes. This helps you react quickly in an emergency.

questions.question: The front brake provides about how much of a motorcycle's total stopping power?
questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: When stopping your motorcycle with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Begin slowing down sooner than normal.
Fit into tighter traffic gaps than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Begin slowing down sooner than normal.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight. This makes the motorcycle slower to speed up, slow down, and turn. Start slowing earlier than usual when carrying a passenger. Also, allow more time for stopping and look for bigger gaps in traffic when merging.

questions.question: When riding in a group, riders should generally use:
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is best for group riding. It keeps riders close while giving each rider enough space. Use single-file when taking curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: Why should a motorcyclist not rely only on mirrors?

options.text: Mirrors can get dirty and block your view.

questions.explanation: You need to be aware of your surroundings. Mirrors alone are not enough. Motorcycles have blind spots, just like other vehicles.

questions.question: If bright sunlight makes it hard to see a motorcycle's turn signals, what should the rider do?

options.text: Keep using the mechanical turn signals.
Honk the horn to warn other drivers about turns.

questions.explanation: Use hand signals when bright sunlight makes your turn signals hard to see. It is very important to tell other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: Riding directly beside another vehicle is:

options.text: Safe because you are in a separate lane.
Good because it blocks the wind.
Not safe because the driver may not see you in their blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not safe because the driver may not see you in their blind spot.
questions.explanation: Do not ride beside other vehicles. You may be in the driver's blind spot. The driver might move into your lane without seeing you.

questions.question: When should you use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch?

options.text: When the throttle is stuck and you cannot free it.
When you start to lose control in a curve.
When the motorcycle starts to wobble.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the throttle is stuck and you cannot free it.
questions.explanation: If the throttle gets stuck and you cannot fix it, use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch right away. This stops power to the rear wheel so you can safely leave the road and stop.

questions.question: The best clothing for a motorcyclist:

options.text: Should not stand out to other drivers.

questions.explanation: Good motorcycle clothing protects you if you crash. It should keep you comfortable and make you visible to other drivers.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: Protects your face, but not your eyes.
Protects your eyes, but not your whole face.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face, including your eyes, in a crash. A windshield is not enough protection.

questions.question: What should you wear when riding during the day?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear clothing with reflective material to be seen, even in daylight. Always wear clothing that covers your arms and legs.

questions.question: What should riders do about blind spots on motorcycles?

options.text: They are nothing to worry about.
They don't exist if you have a rearview mirror.

questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes. Make head checks a regular habit.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop completely and go when it is safe.
Only stop to let other traffic pass.
Vehicles will enter the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop completely, yield to all traffic and pedestrians, and go when it is safe.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT help prevent crashes?

options.text: Be ready to avoid a hazard.
Turn off your headlight during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your headlight during the day.
questions.explanation: To prevent crashes, stay visible to others. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position correctly. Keep space around your motorcycle and always watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT part of a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tires, controls, lights, signals, mirrors, brakes, oil, fluids, chassis, and stands.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A stop sign is coming ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign is coming ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Wear bright, reflective clothing at all times to stay visible to other drivers.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Make it easier for others to see you.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you be seen, avoid hazards and wind blasts, stay out of blind spots, and discourages other drivers from entering your lane. It also gives you a way to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: What gives you the best chance of surviving a crash?
questions.explanation: A helmet that meets DOT and state standards provides the best head and neck protection. Wearing a good-quality, properly fastened helmet is the single best thing you can do to survive a crash.
